subject: Food Science
title: Phage Therapy in Food
description: A micro-lesson that makes Phage Therapy in Food usable.

hook.text: Bacteriophages are viruses that kill bacteria. Spraying them on food could replace antibiotics and chemicals.

buildup.text: Phages are hyper-specific—each type targets one bacterial species while ignoring everything else, including human cells.

discovery.text: ListShield—an FDA-approved phage spray—kills Listeria on deli meats. It's invisible, tasteless, and organic-compatible.

twist.text: Bacteria can evolve resistance to phages too. But new phages can be isolated quickly—faster than developing antibiotics.

climax.text: Phage cocktails targeting Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria are now used in food processing across the US and EU.

punchline.text: Fight bacteria with their own predators. Phages are nature's targeted assassins.

quiz.question: What are bacteriophages?
options: Viruses that specifically target and kill bacteria
